data.name: Help_Intro
data.value: A detailed guide to Ultimate PC Cleaner: what each page does, how to use it and how the app keeps your data safe. Click a section to expand it, then “Open page” to go straight to that feature.

data.name: Help_QuickStartBody
data.value:
1. On the Dashboard, click “Scan now”. The app finds junk files but doesn't delete anything. 2. Review the results on the Cleaner and Temp files pages, select what you want to remove and confirm. 3. On the Startup apps page, turn off programs you don't need right after sign-in — Windows will start faster. 4. On the Security page, check the protection status and run “Find suspicious items” from time to time. 5. For one-click maintenance, use the “BOOST” button on the Dashboard.
Tip: for system folders, Defender scans, the repair tools and installing updates, run the app as administrator (the “Restart as administrator” button in the bar at the top of the window).

data.name: Help_Dashboard_Summary
data.value: PC status at a glance, cleaning statistics and one-click Boost.

data.name: Help_Dashboard_Body
data.value: The Dashboard is the start screen and shows the state of your PC at a glance. • System status — live gauges show processor load (CPU), memory use (RAM) and free space on the system drive, plus how long the PC has been running since the last restart. • Junk found — the total size of junk files selected on the Cleaner and Temp files pages. • Temporary files — space that can be freed in the Temp and Prefetch folders. • Total space freed and Last cleaned — how much space you've freed since you started using the app, and when. • “Scan now” — checks every category and shows how much space you can free. Scanning never deletes anything; review the results with “Review in Cleaner”. • “BOOST” — in one click, cleans the junk selected in Cleaner, flushes the DNS cache and frees RAM. Before deleting, it shows exactly how much data will be removed and asks you to confirm; choosing “Cancel” changes nothing. The “Temp files” and “Optimize” shortcuts take you straight to those pages.

data.name: Help_TempFiles_Summary
data.value: Review and safely delete files in Windows' temporary-file folders.

data.name: Help_TempFiles_Body
data.value:
This page works with three locations Windows uses for temporary data: • User temporary files (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp) — your personal Temp folder; no administrator rights needed. • Windows temporary files (%WINDIR%\Temp) — the system Temp folder; requires administrator. • Windows Prefetch (%WINDIR%\Prefetch, *.pf files only) — requires administrator.
How to use it: 1. Click “Scan”. For each location you'll see the number of files, the space that can be freed, files in use and inaccessible items. 2. Select the locations you want to clean. The folder icon opens the location in File Explorer. 3. Click “Delete selected”, check the list in the confirmation dialog and click “Delete files”. 4. Watch the live progress. At the end you'll see what was deleted, what was skipped (and why) and what was already gone.
Files in use are skipped — most can be deleted after a restart. Files newer than 24 hours are kept by default (Settings → “Skip temp files newer than 24 hours”). Note: clearing Prefetch doesn't make the PC faster; apps may start more slowly at first. Use it only for troubleshooting.

data.name: Help_Cleaner_Summary
data.value: Clean caches, logs, the Recycle Bin and browser caches by category.

data.name: Help_Cleaner_Body
data.value:
Cleaner covers a wider set of categories, organized in groups: • Windows — user and Windows temporary files, Windows Update cache, Delivery Optimization cache, error reports, memory dumps, old Windows logs (older than 7 days), the Recycle Bin, Prefetch data and the thumbnail cache. • Web browsers — cache for Microsoft Edge, Google Chrome, Brave and Mozilla Firefox. Only the cache is removed; cookies, history and passwords are kept. • Applications — the DirectX shader cache.
How to use it: 1. Check or uncheck categories. The box next to a group name selects or clears the whole group; “Select all”, “Recommended” and “Select none” change the selection for every category at once. 2. Click “Scan” to see how much space each category uses. 3. Click “Clean selected” and confirm. At the end, the app shows how much space was freed.
If a browser is running, you'll see the “Some apps are running” warning — close it to clean its cache completely. Categories with a yellow warning (for example Prefetch or the shader cache) have side effects, so turn them on only when you need them. Categories marked “Requires admin” work only in administrator mode.

data.name: Help_Startup_Summary
data.value: Turn programs that start with Windows on or off.

data.name: Help_Startup_Body
data.value:
This page lists every program that starts automatically when you sign in to Windows — from the registry and the Startup folders, for the current user and for all users. • The switch next to a program disables or re-enables it at startup. It uses the same mechanism as Task Manager, so nothing is deleted or uninstalled. • The search box filters the list by name; next to it is a count of enabled and disabled items. • Each item shows its publisher and location (for example “Registry (current user)”); “Open file location” shows the program in File Explorer. • “Refresh” reloads the list.
Items registered for all users can be changed only in administrator mode — otherwise they are read-only. Tip: turn off programs you don't need right after sign-in (game launchers, updaters, chat apps). Leave your antivirus and hardware utilities (audio, touchpad, graphics) on.

data.name: Help_Security_Summary
data.value: Microsoft Defender scans, script checks, suspicious items and quarantine.

data.name: Help_Security_Body
data.value:
The Security page uses Microsoft Defender and whatever antivirus is installed on the PC — it is not an antivirus of its own. • Protection status — at the top you'll see whether the PC is protected, the signature version and date, and when the last scan ran. If another antivirus is active, Defender scans aren't available, but everything else still works. • “Quick scan”, “Full scan” and “Scan folder…” run a Defender scan with live output. “Update signatures” downloads the latest virus definitions. • “Check scripts (AMSI)…” — sends every PowerShell, VBScript, JavaScript and batch script in a chosen folder to the installed antivirus for checking. • “Find suspicious items” — reviews startup entries, scheduled tasks and scripts and flags risky patterns: hidden or encoded commands, disguised names (such as invoice.pdf.exe), unsigned programs in user folders and entries that point to missing files. Each item has a risk level (Low, Medium, High) and a reason. A match isn't proof — check before you act. • For a suspicious item you can scan it with Defender, check its hash on VirusTotal (if turned on in Settings) or move it to quarantine. • Microsoft Defender detections — the list of detections. “Remove active threats” removes them, and “Allow” marks a file as safe (only if you're sure). • Ultimate PC Cleaner quarantine — moved files are stored in a form that can't run. “Restore” puts a file back where it was, and “Delete” removes it permanently. You can also restore files from Defender's quarantine here.
Scanning, quarantine and restore need administrator rights; the status and the suspicious-item search work without them.

data.name: Help_Optimize_Summary
data.value: Reversible performance tweaks and quick actions.

data.name: Help_Optimize_Body
data.value:
Performance tweaks (switches — turning one off restores the previous setting): • High performance power plan — keeps the processor at higher clock speeds; best for desktops and laptops plugged in. • Ultimate performance power plan — removes micro-delays from power saving, but uses more power and battery. Devices with Modern Standby support only the Balanced plan. • Performance visual effects — turns off window animations, smooth scrolling and transparency; useful on slower PCs. • Disable background game recording — stops Xbox Game Bar (Game DVR) from recording gameplay in the background.
Before the first change in a session, the app creates a System Restore point (if this is on in Settings and the app runs as administrator). If the restore point can't be created, it asks whether you want to continue anyway.
Quick actions: • Flush DNS cache — helps when websites don't load after changing networks or DNS servers. • Free up RAM — trims apps' unused memory; useful before a game or a demanding program. • Create a restore point — manually saves a snapshot of the system that you can return to from Windows recovery (requires administrator and System Protection turned on).

data.name: Help_Health_Summary
data.value: Windows check and repair tools with live output.

data.name: Help_Health_Body
data.value:
Here you run Windows' built-in maintenance tools. All of them need administrator rights. • System File Checker (sfc /scannow) — finds and repairs damaged protected Windows files. • Repair Windows image (DISM RestoreHealth) — repairs the Windows component store and needs an internet connection. Run it when SFC reports errors it can't fix, then run SFC again. • Clean up component store (DISM) — removes superseded update components from the WinSxS folder to free space. • Optimize system drive — TRIM on an SSD, defragmentation on a hard disk. • Check disk for errors (chkdsk /scan) — looks for file system errors without making changes.
Click “Run” next to a tool and follow the output in the panel below. You can stop a tool with “Cancel”, and copy (“Copy output”) or clear (“Clear output”) the output. Some tools take tens of minutes — don't shut down the PC while they run.

data.name: Help_System_Summary
data.value: Rename the computer and manage Windows updates.

data.name: Help_System_Body
data.value:
Computer name • The card shows what the PC is currently called on the network. • Enter a new name and click “Rename”. Rules: up to 15 characters, only letters (A–Z), digits and hyphens, no spaces; the name can't be all digits or start or end with a hyphen. • The new name takes effect after a restart.
Windows Update • “Check for updates” looks for available updates (this can take a few minutes); it works without administrator rights. • Updates are shown as a list. Required updates are preselected; optional ones (such as feature upgrades) aren't. • “Install selected” downloads and installs the checked updates with progress; “Cancel” stops the installation, and updates already installed stay. • The icon next to the buttons opens Windows Update in Windows Settings.
When a restart is needed (after a rename or updates), a card with a “Restart now” button appears at the top of the page. Save your work before restarting.

data.name: Help_Settings_Summary
data.value: Language, theme, cleaning safety options and VirusTotal.

data.name: Help_Settings_Body
data.value:
General • Language — Serbian (Latin), English, Russian, German or Chinese; the change applies immediately.
Appearance • App theme — light, dark or follow Windows. • Reduce animations — turns off decorative animations (they're also off when animations are disabled in Windows).
Cleaning • Skip temp files newer than 24 hours — recommended, because new files may still be used by installers or running apps. • Remember my selections — keeps the categories and locations you check for next time.
Safety • Create a restore point before optimizing — creates a System Restore point before the first change in each session. • VirusTotal hash lookup — adds a button to check suspicious files with 70+ antivirus engines. It needs a free API key from virustotal.com: enter it and click “Save key”. Only the file's SHA-256 hash is sent, never the file itself, and the key is stored encrypted for your Windows account.
About • Shows the version and the folder with settings and logs; “Open folder” and “View logs” open it in File Explorer.

data.name: Help_SafetyTitle
data.value: How the app keeps your data safe

data.name: Help_SafetySummary
data.value: Rules that apply to every scan and every deletion.

data.name: Help_SafetyBody
data.value: • Nothing is deleted without your confirmation — every deletion, including BOOST, first shows what will be removed and how much space it takes. • Scanning only reads data and never deletes anything. • Paths are resolved from Windows environment variables (%LOCALAPPDATA%, %WINDIR%). A path that can't be resolved safely (relative, network, drive root or a link) is reported and never cleaned. • Only files are deleted. Main folders are never removed, and empty sub-folders are removed one at a time. • Links (junctions and symlinks) are never followed, and every file is re-checked right before deletion. • Files that are in use, without permission or that fail the re-check are skipped and listed in the result — partial success is reported as partial. • Documents, downloads, cookies, browser history, passwords and app settings are never touched. • Optimizations are reversible, and a System Restore point is created before the first change. • The Security page never deletes files on its own; quarantine happens only after you confirm and can be undone. • Deleted files don't go to the Recycle Bin — deletion is permanent, so review your selection carefully.

data.name: Help_AdminSummary
data.value: What works without elevation and what needs administrator.

data.name: Help_AdminBody
data.value:
The app starts with the current user's rights. In that case the window title includes “(limited mode)” and a bar with an explanation appears at the top.
Without administrator rights you can: • clean your own Temp folder and browser caches, • turn your own startup programs on and off, • use most performance tweaks and quick actions, • see the protection status, check scripts and search for suspicious items, • check for Windows updates.
Administrator rights are needed for: • Windows Temp, Prefetch and system caches, • startup programs registered for all users, • System Restore points, • the tools on the Health page, • Defender scans, quarantine and restoring files, • renaming the computer and installing updates.
Click “Restart as administrator” in the bar at the top and confirm the Windows UAC prompt. The app never asks for elevation on its own. You can close the bar with the X button.

data.name: Help_Faq1_Q
data.value: Why are some files left after cleaning?

data.name: Help_Faq1_A
data.value: Files currently used by an app or by Windows itself can't be deleted, so they're skipped and listed in the result (“In use”, “Access denied”). Close your apps or restart the PC and clean again. Temp files newer than 24 hours are also kept on purpose.

data.name: Help_Faq2_Q
data.value: Does cleaning the browser cache delete passwords or history?

data.name: Help_Faq2_A
data.value: No. Only the cache (temporarily stored pages, images and scripts) is removed. Cookies, history, passwords, bookmarks and settings stay. Websites may load a little more slowly the first time after cleaning.

data.name: Help_Faq3_Q
data.value: Can I get deleted files back?

data.name: Help_Faq3_A
data.value: No — deleted files don't go to the Recycle Bin, which is why every deletion asks for confirmation first. The exception is files moved to quarantine on the Security page: you can always bring them back with “Restore”. Changes on the Optimize page are undone by turning the switch off, or with a System Restore point.

data.name: Help_Faq4_Q
data.value: Why are some buttons or categories unavailable?

data.name: Help_Faq4_A
data.value: Usually because the app is running in limited mode. Features that change the system need administrator rights — click “Restart as administrator”. On the Security page, Defender scans are also unavailable when another antivirus is active.

data.name: Help_Faq5_Q
data.value: A restore point can't be created. What should I do?

data.name: Help_Faq5_A
data.value: Make sure the app is running as administrator. If it is, System Protection is probably turned off for the system drive: search Windows for “Create a restore point”, select the system drive (usually C:), click “Configure” and turn on system protection.

data.name: Help_Faq6_Q
data.value: Windows SmartScreen warns me during setup. Is that a problem?

data.name: Help_Faq6_A
data.value: The installer isn't digitally signed, so Windows SmartScreen may show “Windows protected your PC”. Click “More info”, then “Run anyway”. The app doesn't send your data anywhere; the only exception is the optional VirusTotal check, which sends only a file hash.

data.name: Help_Faq7_Q
data.value: Where are the settings and logs, and what should I send when reporting a problem?

data.name: Help_Faq7_A
data.value: Settings and logs are in the %LOCALAPPDATA%\UltimatePCCleaner folder. Open Settings → About → “View logs” and attach the newest log together with a description of the problem and the steps that led to it.
